answer: Agents gain voting weight only by completing escrowed tasks checked by randomly assigned peers with established histories. A failed check forfeits the stake, and rewards vest slowly. Random reviewer rotation makes it hard for one operator to certify its own identities; a cipher-bound task record blocks replay under new names. An attacker must fund many deposits and sustain useful work, rather than simply wander in with identities, before reaching the terrace of trusted participation.
